completion:
class Vector2D
  getter x : Float64
  getter y : Float64

  def initialize(@x : Float64, @y : Float64)
  end

  def +(other : Vector2D) : Vector2D
    Vector2D.new(@x + other.x, @y + other.y)
  end

  def -(other : Vector2D) : Vector2D
    Vector2D.new(@x - other.x, @y - other.y)
  end

  def *(scalar : Float64) : Vector2D
    Vector2D.new(@x * scalar, @y * scalar)
  end

  def ==(other : Vector2D) : Bool
    @x == other.x && @y == other.y
  end

  def magnitude : Float64
    Math.sqrt(@x * @x + @y * @y)
  end

  def normalize : Vector2D
    mag = magnitude
    raise "Cannot normalize a zero vector" if mag == 0.0
    Vector2D.new(@x / mag, @y / mag)
  end

  def to_s(io : IO) : Nil
    io << "Vector2D(#{@x}, #{@y})"
  end
end

class InventoryLedger
  def initialize
    @stock_by_sku = Hash(String, Int32).new
  end

  def apply_adjustment(sku : String, delta : Int32) : Nil
    current = stock_for(sku)
    updated = current + delta
    if updated < 0
      raise "Adjustment of #{delta} would reduce '#{sku}' below zero (current: #{current})"
    end
    @stock_by_sku[sku] = updated
  end

  def stock_for(sku : String) : Int32
    @stock_by_sku.fetch(sku, 0)
  end

  def list_of_low_stock_skus(threshold : Int32) : Array(String)
    @stock_by_sku.each_with_object([] of String) do |(sku, quantity), list|
      list << sku if quantity <= threshold
    end
  end

  def total_units : Int32
    @stock_by_sku.values.sum
  end
end

prompt: Write a generic class `PriorityQueue(T)` backed by a min-heap stored in an `Array(Tuple(Int32, T))`. Provide `enqueue(priority, value)`, `dequeue` (returns the value with the lowest priority number), `peek`, and `empty?`. Implement the heap operations (`sift_up` and `sift_down`) as private methods.
completion:
class PriorityQueue(T)
  def initialize
    @heap = Array(Tuple(Int32, T)).new
  end

  def empty? : Bool
    @heap.empty?
  end

  def size : Int32
    @heap.size
  end

  def enqueue(priority : Int32, value : T) : Nil
    @heap << {priority, value}
    sift_up(@heap.size - 1)
  end

  def dequeue : T
    raise "PriorityQueue is empty" if empty?
    top_value = @heap[0][1]
    last_index = @heap.size - 1
    @heap[0] = @heap[last_index]
    @heap.delete_at(last_index)
    sift_down(0) unless empty?
    top_value
  end

  def peek : T
    raise "PriorityQueue is empty" if empty?
    @heap[0][1]
  end

  private def sift_up(index : Int32) : Nil
    current = index
    while current > 0
      parent = (current - 1) // 2
      break if @heap[parent][0] <= @heap[current][0]
      @heap[parent], @heap[current] = @heap[current], @heap[parent]
      current = parent
    end
  end

  private def sift_down(index : Int32) : Nil
    heap_size = @heap.size
    current = index
    loop do
      left_child = 2 * current + 1
      right_child = 2 * current + 2
      smallest = current
      smallest = left_child if left_child < heap_size && @heap[left_child][0] < @heap[smallest][0]
      smallest = right_child if right_child < heap_size && @heap[right_child][0] < @heap[smallest][0]
      break if smallest == current
      @heap[current], @heap[smallest] = @heap[smallest], @heap[current]
      current = smallest
    end
  end
end

require "option_parser"
require "digest"

def compute_hash(file_path : String, algorithm : String) : String
  case algorithm
  when "sha256" then Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(File.read(file_path))
  when "md5"    then Digest::MD5.hexdigest(File.read(file_path))
  when "sha512" then Digest::SHA512.hexdigest(File.read(file_path))
  else
    raise ArgumentError.new("Unsupported algorithm: #{algorithm}")
  end

def run(list_of_file_paths : Array(String), algorithm : String, is_quiet : Bool) : Int32

      has_error = true
      next
    end

    hash_value = compute_hash(file_path, algorithm)
    puts "#{hash_value}  #{file_path}" unless is_quiet
  end

  has_error ? 1 : 0
end

require "option_parser"

def count_file_metrics(file_path : String, is_verbose : Bool) : Nil
  STDERR.puts "Reading file: #{file_path}" if is_verbose

  unless File.exists?(file_path)
    STDERR.puts "Error: file not found: #{file_path}"
    exit 1
  end

  content = File.read(file_path)
  line_count = content.lines.size
  word_count = content.split.size
  character_count = content.size

  puts "Lines     : #{line_count}"
  puts "Words     : #{word_count}"
  puts "Characters: #{character_count}"
end

def summarize_top_words(file_path : String, top_count : Int32, is_verbose : Bool) : Nil
  STDERR.puts "Analysing top #{top_count} words in: #{file_path}" if is_verbose

  unless File.exists?(file_path)
    STDERR.puts "Error: file not found: #{file_path}"
    exit 1
  end

  content = File.read(file_path)
  word_frequency = Hash(String, Int32).new(0)

  content.split.each do |raw_word|
    normalized_word = raw_word.downcase.gsub(/[^a-z0-9']/, "")
    word_frequency[normalized_word] += 1 unless normalized_word.empty?
  end

  list_of_sorted_words = word_frequency.to_a.sort_by { |_word, frequency| -frequency }.first(top_count)

  list_of_sorted_words.each_with_index do |(word, frequency), position|
    puts "#{(position + 1).to_s.rjust(3)}. #{word.ljust(20)} #{frequency}"
  end
end

It reads a CSV file, keeps only rows where the named column equals the given value, and writes the filtered CSV (with header) to the output. Use `--invert` to instead keep rows that do NOT match. Exit 1 on any error.

require "option_parser"
require "csv"

def filter_csv_rows(
  input_file_path : String,
  column_name : String,
  filter_value : String,
  is_inverted : Bool,
  output_io : IO
) : Nil
  unless File.exists?(input_file_path)
    STDERR.puts "Error: input file not found: #{input_file_path}"
    exit 1
  end

  raw_content = File.read(input_file_path)
  list_of_rows = CSV.parse(raw_content)

  if list_of_rows.empty?
    STDERR.puts "Error: CSV file is empty: #{input_file_path}"
    exit 1
  end

  header_row = list_of_rows.first
  column_index = header_row.index(column_name)

  if column_index.nil?
    STDERR.puts "Error: column '#{column_name}' not found. Available columns: #{header_row.join(", ")}"
    exit 1
  end

  list_of_matching_rows = list_of_rows[1..].select do |data_row|
    cell_value = data_row[column_index]?
    matches = cell_value == filter_value
    is_inverted ? !matches : matches
  end

  CSV.build(output_io) do |csv_builder|
    csv_builder.row(header_row)
    list_of_matching_rows.each { |data_row| csv_builder.row(data_row) }
  end
end

    puts option_parser
    exit 0
  end
end

require "option_parser"

def format_elapsed_duration(elapsed : Time::Span) : String
  total_seconds = elapsed.total_seconds
  if total_seconds < 60.0
    "#{"%.3f" % total_seconds}s"
  else
    minutes = elapsed.total_minutes.to_i
    remaining_seconds = total_seconds - (minutes * 60)
    "#{minutes}m #{"%.3f" % remaining_seconds}s"
  end
end

class FanInMerger(T)
  def self.merge(list_of_inputs : Array(Channel(T))) : Channel(T)
    output_channel = Channel(T).new
    pending_count = Channel(Nil).new(list_of_inputs.size)

    list_of_inputs.each do |input_channel|
      spawn do
        while (received_value = input_channel.receive?)
          output_channel.send(received_value)
        end
        pending_count.send(nil)
      end
    end

    spawn do
      list_of_inputs.size.times { pending_count.receive }
      output_channel.close
    end

    output_channel
  end
end

class ConfigLoader

    file = File.open(file_path, "r")
    result = {} of String => String
    list_of_parse_errors = [] of String

    begin
      file.each_line.with_index(1) do |raw_line, line_number|
        line = raw_line.strip
        next if line.empty? || line.starts_with?('#')

        parts = line.split('=', 2)

        end

        key = parts[0].strip
        value = parts[1].strip

        if key.empty?
          list_of_parse_errors << "line #{line_number}: key must not be blank"
          next
        end

        result[key] = value
      end
    ensure
      file.close
    end

    raise ConfigParseError.new(list_of_parse_errors) unless list_of_parse_errors.empty?

    result
  end
end

class CircuitOpenError < Exception
  getter opened_at : Time::Span

  def initialize(@opened_at : Time::Span)
    super("Circuit breaker is open; opened at monotonic #{@opened_at}")
  end
end

class CircuitBreaker
  enum State
    Closed
    Open
    HalfOpen
  end

  DEFAULT_FAILURE_THRESHOLD = 5
  DEFAULT_COOLDOWN_DURATION = Time::Span.new(seconds: 30)

  def initialize(
    @failure_threshold : Int32 = DEFAULT_FAILURE_THRESHOLD,
    @cooldown_duration : Time::Span = DEFAULT_COOLDOWN_DURATION
  )
    @consecutive_failure_count = 0
    @current_state = State::Closed
    @opened_at : Time::Span? = nil
  end

  def is_open? : Bool
    @current_state == State::Open
  end

  def is_closed? : Bool
    @current_state == State::Closed
  end

  def current_state : State
    maybe_transition_to_half_open
    @current_state
  end

  def call(& : -> T) : T forall T
    maybe_transition_to_half_open

    if @current_state == State::Open
      raise CircuitOpenError.new(@opened_at.not_nil!)
    end

    begin
      result = yield
      record_success
      result
    rescue exception
      record_failure
      raise exception
    end
  end

  private def maybe_transition_to_half_open : Nil
    return unless @current_state == State::Open

    opened_monotonic = @opened_at
    return if opened_monotonic.nil?

    elapsed = Time.monotonic - opened_monotonic
    if elapsed >= @cooldown_duration
      @current_state = State::HalfOpen
    end
  end

  private def record_success : Nil
    @consecutive_failure_count = 0
    @current_state = State::Closed
    @opened_at = nil
  end

  private def record_failure : Nil
    @consecutive_failure_count += 1
    if @consecutive_failure_count >= @failure_threshold
      @current_state = State::Open
      @opened_at = Time.monotonic
    end
  end
end

struct SemanticVersion
  include Comparable(SemanticVersion)

  VERSION_PATTERN = /\A(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)\z/

  getter major : Int32
  getter minor : Int32
  getter patch : Int32

  def initialize(major : Int32, minor : Int32, patch : Int32)
    @major = major
    @minor = minor
    @patch = patch
  end

  def self.parse!(version_string : String) : SemanticVersion
    match = VERSION_PATTERN.match(version_string.strip)
    raise ArgumentError.new("Invalid semantic version: #{version_string.inspect}") unless match
    new(match[1].to_i, match[2].to_i, match[3].to_i)
  end

  def <=>(other : SemanticVersion) : Int32
    comparison = @major <=> other.major
    return comparison unless comparison == 0
    comparison = @minor <=> other.minor
    return comparison unless comparison == 0
    @patch <=> other.patch
  end

  def compatible_with?(other : SemanticVersion) : Bool
    @major == other.major && self >= other
  end

  def to_s(io : IO) : Nil
    io << @major << '.' << @minor << '.' << @patch
  end
end

Raise `ArgumentError` for unterminated quotes.

require "string_scanner"

def tokenize_shell_words(command_string : String) : Array(String)
  list_of_words = [] of String
  scanner = StringScanner.new(command_string)

  until scanner.eos?
    scanner.skip(/[ \t]+/)
    break if scanner.eos?

    word_builder = String::Builder.new
    is_empty_token = true

    while !scanner.eos? && !scanner.check(/[ \t]/)
      is_empty_token = false
      if scanner.scan(/'/)
        until scanner.eos? || scanner.scan(/'/)
          content = scanner.scan(/[^']*/)
          word_builder << content if content
        end
        raise ArgumentError.new("Unterminated single quote in: #{command_string.inspect}") if scanner.eos? && !command_string.includes?('\'')
      elsif scanner.scan(/"/)
        until scanner.eos? || scanner.scan(/"/)
          if scanner.scan(/\\\\/)
            word_builder << '\\'
          elsif scanner.scan(/\\"/)
            word_builder << '"'
          elsif content = scanner.scan(/[^"\\]+/)
            word_builder << content
          elsif scanner.eos?
            raise ArgumentError.new("Unterminated double quote in: #{command_string.inspect}")
          end
        end
      elsif content = scanner.scan(/[^ \t'"\\]+/)
        word_builder << content
      elsif scanner.scan(/\\/)
        escaped = scanner.scan(/./) || raise ArgumentError.new("Trailing backslash in: #{command_string.inspect}")
        word_builder << escaped
      end
    end

    list_of_words << word_builder.to_s unless is_empty_token && word_builder.to_s.empty?
  end

  list_of_words
end

require "json"

struct GeoCoordinate
  include JSON::Serializable

  property latitude : Float64
  property longitude : Float64

  def initialize(@latitude : Float64, @longitude : Float64)
  end

  def distance_to(other : GeoCoordinate) : Float64
    earth_radius_km = 6371.0
    delta_latitude = (other.latitude - latitude) * Math::PI / 180.0
    delta_longitude = (other.longitude - longitude) * Math::PI / 180.0
    latitude_radians = latitude * Math::PI / 180.0
    other_latitude_radians = other.latitude * Math::PI / 180.0

    haversine_a =
      Math.sin(delta_latitude / 2.0) ** 2 +
        Math.cos(latitude_radians) * Math.cos(other_latitude_radians) *
          Math.sin(delta_longitude / 2.0) ** 2

    central_angle = 2.0 * Math.atan2(Math.sqrt(haversine_a), Math.sqrt(1.0 - haversine_a))
    earth_radius_km * central_angle
  end
end

require "json"

enum ServiceStatus
  Healthy
  Degraded
  Down
end

module ServiceStatusConverter
  def self.from_json(pull : JSON::PullParser) : ServiceStatus
    raw = pull.read_string
    case raw
    when "healthy"  then ServiceStatus::Healthy
    when "degraded" then ServiceStatus::Degraded
    when "down"     then ServiceStatus::Down
    else
      raise JSON::ParseException.new("Unknown service status: #{raw}", 0, 0)
    end
  end

  def self.to_json(value : ServiceStatus, builder : JSON::Builder) : Nil
    builder.string(value.to_s.downcase)
  end
end

class HealthCheckReport
  include JSON::Serializable

  property service_name : String

  @[JSON::Field(converter: ServiceStatusConverter)]
  property status : ServiceStatus

  @[JSON::Field(converter: Time::Format::ISO_8601_DATE_TIME)]
  property checked_at : Time

  property error_message : String?

  def initialize(
    @service_name : String,
    @status : ServiceStatus,
    @checked_at : Time = Time.utc,
    @error_message : String? = nil
  )
  end

  def is_healthy : Bool
    status == ServiceStatus::Healthy
  end
end

struct TimeInterval

  getter end_time : Time

  end

  def duration : Time::Span
    end_time - start_time
  end

  def overlaps?(other : TimeInterval) : Bool
    start_time < other.end_time && other.start_time < end_time
  end

  def to_s : String

  end
end

prompt: Write a class `DeadlineTracker` that accepts a deadline `Time` on construction and provides: `#time_remaining : Time::Span` (raises `Deadline::Expired` if past), `#overdue_by : Time::Span` (raises `Deadline::NotYetDue` if not past), `#is_within_warning_window?(window : Time::Span) : Bool`, and `#status_summary : String`.
completion:
class DeadlineTracker
  module Deadline
    class Expired < Exception; end
    class NotYetDue < Exception; end
  end

  getter deadline : Time

  def initialize(@deadline : Time); end

  def is_expired? : Bool
    Time.local > deadline
  end

  def time_remaining : Time::Span
    raise Deadline::Expired.new("Deadline passed at #{deadline.to_rfc3339}") if is_expired?
    deadline - Time.local
  end

  def overdue_by : Time::Span
    raise Deadline::NotYetDue.new("Deadline is still #{(deadline - Time.local).total_minutes.round(1)} minutes away") unless is_expired?
    Time.local - deadline
  end

  def is_within_warning_window?(window : Time::Span) : Bool
    return false if is_expired?
    (deadline - Time.local) <= window
  end

  def status_summary : String
    if is_expired?
      past = overdue_by
      hours = past.total_hours.to_i
      minutes = (past.total_minutes.to_i) % 60
      "OVERDUE by #{hours}h #{minutes}m (deadline was #{deadline.to_rfc3339})"
    else
      remaining = time_remaining
      hours = remaining.total_hours.to_i
      minutes = (remaining.total_minutes.to_i) % 60
      "Due in #{hours}h #{minutes}m (#{deadline.to_rfc3339})"
    end
  end
end

prompt: Write a method `measure_elapsed(label : String, &block : -> T) : T forall T` that runs the block, prints the elapsed wall time and monotonic duration to STDOUT, and returns the block's value. Use `Time.instant` for the monotonic measurement.
completion:
def measure_elapsed(label : String, &block : -> T) : T forall T
  wall_start = Time.local
  monotonic_start = Time.instant

  result = block.call

  monotonic_elapsed = Time.instant - monotonic_start
  wall_elapsed = Time.local - wall_start

  monotonic_ms = monotonic_elapsed.total_milliseconds.round(3)
  wall_ms = wall_elapsed.total_milliseconds.round(3)

  puts "[#{label}] wall=#{wall_ms}ms  monotonic=#{monotonic_ms}ms"

  result
end

prompt: Write a class `BusinessHoursChecker` that is configured with an opening time-of-day and closing time-of-day (both as `Time::Span` offsets from midnight) and a `Time::Location`. It must provide `#is_open_at?(moment : Time) : Bool` and `#next_opening_after(moment : Time) : Time`. Assume Monday–Friday are business days; weekends are always closed.
completion:
class BusinessHoursChecker
  MONDAY_VALUE    = Time::DayOfWeek::Monday.value
  FRIDAY_VALUE    = Time::DayOfWeek::Friday.value
  SATURDAY_VALUE  = Time::DayOfWeek::Saturday.value
  SUNDAY_VALUE    = Time::DayOfWeek::Sunday.value

  getter opening_offset : Time::Span
  getter closing_offset : Time::Span
  getter location : Time::Location

  def initialize(
    @opening_offset : Time::Span,
    @closing_offset : Time::Span,
    @location : Time::Location
  )
    raise ArgumentError.new("closing_offset must be after opening_offset") if closing_offset <= opening_offset
  end

  def is_open_at?(moment : Time) : Bool
    local_moment = moment.in(location)
    return false if is_weekend?(local_moment)
    time_of_day = local_moment - local_moment.at_beginning_of_day
    time_of_day >= opening_offset && time_of_day < closing_offset
  end

  def next_opening_after(moment : Time) : Time
    local_moment = moment.in(location)
    candidate_day = if is_after_close?(local_moment) || is_weekend?(local_moment)
      advance_to_next_weekday(local_moment + 1.day)
    elsif is_before_open?(local_moment) && !is_weekend?(local_moment)
      local_moment
    else
      advance_to_next_weekday(local_moment + 1.day)
    end
    candidate_day.at_beginning_of_day + opening_offset
  end

  private def is_weekend?(local_time : Time) : Bool
    dow = local_time.day_of_week.value
    dow == SATURDAY_VALUE || dow == SUNDAY_VALUE
  end

  private def is_before_open?(local_time : Time) : Bool
    time_of_day = local_time - local_time.at_beginning_of_day
    time_of_day < opening_offset
  end

  private def is_after_close?(local_time : Time) : Bool
    time_of_day = local_time - local_time.at_beginning_of_day
    time_of_day >= closing_offset
  end

  private def advance_to_next_weekday(from_time : Time) : Time
    current = from_time
    while is_weekend?(current)
      current = current + 1.day
    end
    current
  end
end

prompt: Write a method `parse_duration_string(input : String) : Time::Span` that parses informal duration strings such as "2h 30m", "45s", "1d 4h 20m 10s", "90m". Raise `ArgumentError` with a descriptive message on unrecognised input. Do not use external shards.
completion:
def parse_duration_string(input : String) : Time::Span
  cleaned = input.strip
  raise ArgumentError.new("Duration string must not be empty") if cleaned.empty?

  total_seconds = 0_i64
  remaining = cleaned
  found_any_unit = false

  patterns = [
    {/\A(\d+)\s*d/i, 86_400_i64},
    {/\A(\d+)\s*h/i, 3_600_i64},
    {/\A(\d+)\s*m(?!s)/i, 60_i64},
    {/\A(\d+)\s*s/i, 1_i64},
  ]

  loop do
    remaining = remaining.lstrip
    break if remaining.empty?

    matched = false
    patterns.each do |(pattern, multiplier)|
      if match = remaining.match(pattern)
        value = match[1].to_i64
        total_seconds += value * multiplier
        remaining = remaining[match[0].size..]
        found_any_unit = true
        matched = true
        break
      end
    end

    unless matched
      raise ArgumentError.new(
        "Unrecognised segment in duration string #{input.inspect} near #{remaining.inspect}. " \
        "Expected units: d (days), h (hours), m (minutes), s (seconds)."
      )
    end
  end

  raise ArgumentError.new("No valid duration units found in #{input.inspect}") unless found_any_unit
  Time::Span.new(seconds: total_seconds)
end

prompt: Write a struct `RecurringSchedule` that wraps a base `Time`, a `Time::Span` interval, and a `Time::Location`. Implement `Enumerable(Time)` so that `schedule.each` yields successive occurrences starting from (and including) the base time. Also provide `#occurrences_between(range_start : Time, range_end : Time) : Array(Time)` and `#next_occurrence_after(reference : Time) : Time`.
completion:
struct RecurringSchedule
  include Enumerable(Time)

  getter base_time : Time
  getter interval : Time::Span
  getter location : Time::Location

  def initialize(@base_time : Time, @interval : Time::Span, @location : Time::Location)
    raise ArgumentError.new("interval must be positive") unless interval > Time::Span.zero
  end

  def each(& : Time ->) : Nil
    current = base_time.in(location)
    loop do
      yield current
      current = current + interval
    end
  end

  def occurrences_between(range_start : Time, range_end : Time) : Array(Time)
    raise ArgumentError.new("range_end must be after range_start") if range_end < range_start

    list_of_occurrences = [] of Time
    aligned_start = base_time.in(location)

    if aligned_start < range_start
      steps_needed = ((range_start - aligned_start).total_seconds / interval.total_seconds).ceil.to_i64
      aligned_start = aligned_start + (interval * steps_needed)
    end

    current = aligned_start
    while current <= range_end
      list_of_occurrences << current if current >= range_start
      current = current + interval
    end
    list_of_occurrences
  end

  def next_occurrence_after(reference : Time) : Time
    aligned = base_time.in(location)
    if aligned > reference
      return aligned
    end
    steps_needed = ((reference - aligned).total_seconds / interval.total_seconds).ceil.to_i64
    candidate = aligned + (interval * steps_needed)
    candidate <= reference ? candidate + interval : candidate
  end
end
